NECROTIZING_FASCIITIS.title: Necrotizing fasciitis (rapidly spreading deep skin infection)

items: Necrotizing fasciitis is a serious infection that spreads quickly through the layers under the skin, causing tissue death.
Pain that is out of proportion to what the skin looks like.
Skin that is red, swollen, or becomes numb or dark, and sometimes blisters or crackling under the skin.
Feeling very unwell, with fever and low blood pressure.
Surgical exploration of the area, which is both a test and a treatment.
Blood cultures and tissue cultures taken during surgery.
Blood tests including creatine kinase (CK) and a risk score.
Surgery to remove dead tissue is usually needed, with antibiotics into a vein.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Do not wait. Go to hospital straight away if pain is out of proportion to the skin appearance.
Repeat surgery or dressings may be needed. Your team will explain the plan.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Pain out of proportion to the skin, or skin going dark, blue, or numb (emergency: immediate treatment is required)
Low blood pressure, fainting, or confusion
